title: Her run-in with Schiffman over booking with John Kirby at the Apollo
summary: She skipped an Apollo opening billed with Kirby because she was newly remarried, and Schiffman retaliated; she never played the Apollo again.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: You also told another story involving --
Oh yeah, I had a --
......booking you with John Kirby.

I had a personal run-in with Schiffman, because after Kirby and I were separated and divorced, Kirby was going in his direction and I in mine. And I happened to have been appearing at Le Ruban Bleu in New York, and I hadn't appeared at the Apollo for quite some time. So Schiffman came down the Le Ruban Bleu and asked me if I would be interested in playing at the Apollo Theater. And I told him yeah, but there was a stipulation. I mentioned the fact that under no circumstances did I want to appear at the Apollo

Theater billed with John Kirby.
This was for the simple reason that I --
at the time I was married again and I didn't want
to cause any friction, you know, family-wise.
Because when you play Harlem, the press
and the theater have a tendency to put two and two
together, and they might've made more out of it
than really what existed.
So therefore, I made that stipulation.
And that was, oh, months before the date that we
were supposed -- that I was supposed to appear.
And, of course, Schiffman assured me
that this would never happen, because we brought
out the fact that you know, there are at least forty
working weeks in the year for theatrical performers,
and they never have to cross paths.
So I was pretty confident that everything
was going to be all right.
However, the night before I was to
open, I was at the Le Ruban Bleu at the time, and
one of my co-workers -- I was on a bill with an
act, Day, Dawn and Dusk. And Eddie Coman who was the
pianist, said, "I see you're opening at the Apollo tomorrow with John Kirby." I said, "Oh no, can't be!"
So after I got off from work, I drove by the theater. And sure enough, on the marquee, they had "Maxine Sullivan and John Kirby Appearing For The First Time Since Their Divorce." And I was furious!
I can imagine.
Oh yeah.
So I didn't show up for the rehearsal the next morning. You usually rehearse the show in the morning.
So Schiffman sent for me, and I went down and I told him, I said, "Well under no circumstances will I appear." I said, "Because our understanding was that this would never happen."

And, of course, then he went on to tell me about how Jack Benny and Mary Livingston worked together and they hadn't spoken for years. And, of course, I had to tell him I had absolutely nothing to do with Jack Benny and Mary Livingston's

business -- that I wouldn't appear.
So I didn't. I think they got a
singer, Avis Andrews, who was a very good singer
at that time. I think she had sung with Duke
Ellington.

And she opened and appeared with the
band that week. I never did know what the outcome
was, because by that time I was so angry, I didn't
even want to know.

But I'm pretty sure that that had a
lot to do with my not appearing at the Apollo
Theater, you know. Anymore from that time on until
the time that the Apollo Theater closed.

These are some of the things that
could happen. I don't know -- I don't think that
this is a universal thing, but it happened in that
particular case. So, that was another one of those
experiences.

I tried to -- I've never had any sort
of problem about not showing up on an engagement,
or breaking contracts -- things like that.
And I certainly wouldn't want anything
